extracted.intended_audience: NIH/NLM grant applicants (principal investigators) considering an appeal of peer review or referral decisions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how a principal investigator may appeal procedural aspects of NIH/NLM grant peer review or referral decisions, and the internal steps, timing, and possible outcomes of that appeals process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an appeal / eligible grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: "With regard to the initial review, after examining the summary statement containing the results of that review for the grant application, an investigator may have concerns about, and wish to contest a procedural aspect of the process (e.g., that the review was biased, that conflict of interest existed, that the review group lacked appropriate expertise, that factual errors entered into the review)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This wording is taken from the NIH Guide Notice (dated November 21, 1997) which provides full information on NIH policy on 'Appeals of Scientific Peer Review.' Examples of eligible procedural complaints include bias, conflict of interest, lack of appropriate expertise, or factual errors in the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult the NLM program officer before appealing
rubrics_metrics.description: Before beginning the appeal process, the principal investigator is strongly advised to speak with their National Library of Medicine (NLM) program officer, who is listed on the summary statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program officer can explain options and their consequences, help the applicant understand the study section's comments and recommendation, and in most cases peer review issues can be resolved at this stage. Use this conversation as the first step because many issues are resolved without formal appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: First formal step: submission of an appeal letter
rubrics_metrics.description: For cases that cannot be resolved by discussion, the first step is the submission of an appeal letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appeal letter submitted after study section review should be sent to the program officer in NLM. Program and review staff will try to resolve the issues and take the appropriate action; if unresolved, the appeal letter and all relevant information are submitted to the Appeals Officer/Deputy Director for Research & Education, NLM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirement for Council consideration (six-week rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal letter and all relevant information are submitted to the Appeals Officer/Deputy Director for Research & Education, NLM, six weeks before the next Council meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the letter is not received sufficiently in advance of the Council meeting, it may be necessary to delay Council consideration of an appeal until the following Council meeting. Ensure timely submission to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals Officer decision and possible referral to Council
rubrics_metrics.description: The Appeals Officer decides if the appeal needs to go to Council for further consideration. If Council review is warranted, it will be presented to the Board of Regents of the National Library of Medicine for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Appeals Officer/Deputy Director evaluates the materials and determines whether Council should review the appeal; not all appeals will be forwarded to Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible Council outcomes and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council may agree with either the study section or the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Council agrees with the applicant, it recommends appropriate actions to resolve the matter, which may include re-review of the application. If the Council concurs with the study section recommendation, the application will not be re-reviewed, but a revised application may be submitted. The program officer can often give valuable advice about revising an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals of receipt and referral issues for unreviewed applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals of receipt and referral issues regarding applications not yet reviewed should be directed to the Referral Office, Center for Scientific Review (formerly, Division of Research Grants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipt/referral complaints follow a different route than appeals of initial peer review; consult the Referral Office/Center for Scientific Review and relevant OER Grants/Extramural Policy Notices for procedures and policy details.
